lesson.title: Start from a problem
lesson.subtitle: From a school problem to a plan people agree on

video.title: Start from a problem
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma — maths teacher (opens the lesson)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Ms Salma opens a staffroom cupboard; a dusty box of sensors sits on the shelf, still sealed.
scenes.animation: Cupboard door swings open; dust drifts off the box.
scenes.narration: A school near us was given a box of smart sensors. A year later, it's still in a cupboard. Nobody had asked what problem they would solve. Today we start the other way round: from the problem.

scenes.visual: Darsi title card with the IoT track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: start a smart school project from a problem, not a gadget.

scenes.visual: A water tank on a tower behind a school; a dry tap in the toilets. Pupils, a cleaner and the caretaker look up at it.
scenes.animation: The tap drips once and stops; the people appear one by one.
scenes.narration: Start from a problem people feel. Our water tank runs dry without warning, two or three times a term. Ask who it hurts: pupils, cleaners, the caretaker who checks it. Talk to them before choosing anything.

scenes.visual: Two speech bubbles: a cloudy one saying 'a smarter school' and a sharp one with a falling line on a small chart.
scenes.animation: The cloudy bubble fades; the sharp one draws its line.
scenes.narration: Next, turn it into a question you can measure. A smarter school is a wish: no sensor can answer it. How fast does the water level fall, and on which days? That, a sensor can answer.

scenes.visual: A term calendar with five days crossed in red; then an empty calendar with a green target.
scenes.animation: Red crosses stamp in; the second calendar stays clean.
scenes.on_screen_text: Success: a number and a date
scenes.narration: Then write a success measure: a number and a date. Last term, the tank ran dry on five days. Goal: none by the end of term, with a day's warning.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor holds up a sheet that reads 'the water problem gets better'. Two answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A colleague's success measure: the water problem gets better. Good enough?

scenes.visual: The vague sheet gets three question marks; it is rewritten with a number and a date.
scenes.animation: Question marks pop; the new line writes itself in.
scenes.on_screen_text: Add a number and a date
scenes.narration: Not good enough: you could never tell whether it worked. Better for whom, by how much, by when? Say: no dry days by the end of term.

scenes.visual: A cut-away of the tank: a sensor on the lid sends a pulse down to the water. Beside it, a battery, a small solar panel and three radio icons.
scenes.animation: The pulse bounces off the water; the options slide in.
scenes.narration: Now choose the parts. A waterproof distance sensor on the lid measures how far down the water is. Power: batteries, or a battery and a small solar panel. Network: Wi-Fi if it reaches, a mobile SIM, or LoRa.

scenes.visual: A grid on the board: three options down the side, four criteria across, scores in each cell. The caretaker points at the upkeep column.
scenes.animation: Scores fill in; the upkeep weight grows from 2 to 5.
scenes.narration: Weigh the options in a decision matrix. Score each on cost, upkeep, range and power. Weight each, multiply and add up. And agree the weights with the people affected: the caretaker cares most about upkeep.

scenes.visual: A price tag on a sensor, then a stack of monthly bills, a pile of batteries and a ladder against the tank.
scenes.animation: Each cost drops onto a growing pile.
scenes.on_screen_text: The price is not the cost
scenes.narration: Count every cost, not just the price. A SIM's data plan costs money every month. Batteries need changing. And someone must climb up to clean and fix things.

scenes.visual: A single sheet pinned to the staffroom wall, with four boxes filling in. Pupils' names appear beside the roles.
scenes.animation: Each box fills as it is said.
scenes.narration: Then put it all on one page: the problem, question and success measure. The parts, the cost, and who pays. A timeline, with a pilot first. And roles for pupils: builders, testers, a data team and reporters.

scenes.visual: Amina beside a board with a scored grid; the caretaker walks past in the corridor. Two answer cards bounce in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. My class scored three designs, and LoRa won. Nobody asked the caretaker, who'll change its batteries. Is our choice made?

scenes.visual: Four icons line up: a tank, a question mark, a calendar, a balance.
scenes.narration: Not yet: the weights are a judgement, and the caretaker lives with the result. Ask him, then score again. Remember: a problem people feel, a measurable question, a number and a date, and choices weighed together.

scenes.visual: Groups at desks with sheets of paper; the board fills with problems and tally marks.
scenes.animation: Tally marks add up beside one problem; it gets a circle.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: a problem hunt. Groups list three school problems, who each hurts, and what to measure. The class votes for one, and drafts its one-page plan. Next time: pilot one sensor before building many.

checkpoints.prompt: Success measure: the water problem gets better. Good enough?

options.text: No — it needs a number and a date

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — with no number and no date, nobody can tell whether it worked.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — nobody can check whether it got better. Add a number and a date: no dry days by the end of term.

checkpoints.prompt: Pupils scored three designs, but nobody asked the caretaker who will look after it. Is the choice made?

options.text: No — agree the weights with him

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the weights are a judgement, so the people who live with the system help set them.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the numbers only repeat the weights you chose. Ask the caretaker, then score again.
